arxiv-2103-10062.title: From one-way streets to percolation on random mixed graphs
arxiv-2103-10062.creator: Vincent Verbavatz, Marc Barthelemy
arxiv-2103-10062.description: Abstract In most studies, street networks are considered as undirected graphs while one-way streets and their effect on shortest paths are usually ignored. Here, we first study the empirical effect of one-way streets in about 140 140 cities in the world. Their presence induces a detour that persists over a wide range of distances and characterized by a non-universal exponent.

arxiv-2104-01052.title: An Evaluation of the Archive of Formal Proofs
arxiv-2104-01052.creator: Carlin MacKenzie, Jacques Fleuriot, James Vaughan
arxiv-2104-01052.description: Abstract 1 Introduction The Archive of Formal Proofs (AFP) is an online repository of formal proofs for the Isabelle proof assistant 1 1 1 https://isabelle.in.tum.de . It first appeared on the internet in 2004, hosted as a static site on SourceForge 2 2 2 https://afp.sourceforge.net , to serve as a central location for publishing, discovering, and viewing libraries of proofs.

arxiv-2109-04209.title: Revisiting Cosmologies in Teleparallelism
arxiv-2109-04209.creator: Fabio D’Ambrosio, Lavinia Heisenberg, Simon Kuhn
arxiv-2109-04209.description: Abstract We discuss the most general field equations for cosmological spacetimes for theories of gravity based on non-linear extensions of the non-metricity scalar and the torsion scalar. Our approach is based on a systematic symmetry-reduction of the metric-affine geometry which underlies these theories.

arxiv-2207-11233.title: E2N: Error Estimation Networks for Goal-Oriented Mesh Adaptation Journal: Journal of Computational Physics
arxiv-2207-11233.creator: Joseph G. Wallwork, Jingyi Lu, Mingrui Zhang, Matthew D. Piggott
arxiv-2207-11233.description: Abstract Given a partial differential equation (PDE), goal-oriented error estimation allows us to understand how errors in a diagnostic quantity of interest (QoI), or goal , occur and accumulate in a numerical approximation, for example using the finite element method.

arxiv-2401-10159.title: Derivations and the first Hochschild cohomology group of the quantum grassmannian This research was partly supported by EPSRC grant EP/R009279/1.
arxiv-2401-10159.creator: S Launois, T H Lenagan
arxiv-2401-10159.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by S Launois, T H Lenagan. We calculate the derivations and the first Hochschild cohomology group of the quantum grassmannian over a field of characteristic zero in the generic case when the deformation parameter is not a root of unity. Using graded techniques and two special homogeneous normal elements of the quantum grassmannian, we reduce the problem to computing derivations of the quantum grassmannian that act trivially on these two normal elements.

arxiv-2404-07091.title: LaTiM: Longitudinal representation learning in continuous-time models to predict disease progression
arxiv-2404-07091.creator: Rachid Zeghlache, Pierre-Henri Conze, Mostafa El Habib Daho, Yihao Li, Hugo Le Boité, Ramin Tadayoni, Pascal Massin, Béatrice Cochener, Alireza Rezaei, Ikram Brahim, Gwenolé Quellec, Mathieu Lamard
arxiv-2404-07091.description: Abstract This work proposes a novel framework for analyzing disease progression using time-aware neural ordinary differential equations (NODE). We introduce a "time-aware head" in a framework trained through self-supervised learning (SSL) to leverage temporal information in latent space for data augmentation.

pmc-10671449.title: Environmental Causes of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
pmc-10671449.creator: Sheiphali Gandhi, Roberto Tonelli, Margaret Murray, Anna Valeria Samarelli, Paolo Spagnolo, Cristina Porta, Francesca Bodega
pmc-10671449.description: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), the most common and severe of the idiopathic interstitial pneumonias, is a chronic and relentlessly progressive disease, which occurs mostly in middle-aged and elderly males. Although IPF is by definition “idiopathic”, multiple factors have been reported to increase disease risk, aging being the most prominent one.

pmc-11354297.title: Balanced Duality: H2O2-Based Therapy in Cancer and Its Protective Effects on Non-Malignant Tissues
pmc-11354297.creator: Amira Zaher, Michael S. Petronek, Bryan G. Allen, Kranti A. Mapuskar
pmc-11354297.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Conventional cancer therapy strategies, although centered around killing tumor cells, often lead to severe side effects on surrounding normal tissues, thus compromising the chronic quality of life in cancer survivors. Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) is a secondary signaling molecule that has an array of functions in both tumor and normal cells, including the promotion of cell survival pathways and immune cell modulation in the tumor microenvironment.

pmc-11666840.title: Oviductus Ranae Promotes Follicle Growth Through the PI3K/AKT Signaling Pathway In Vivo and In Vitro in Rat
pmc-11666840.creator: Hongyu Zhao, Yu Wang, Xueyuan Sun, Xingyao He, Lin Di, Zhen Yang
pmc-11666840.description: The development status of follicles determines the menstrual cycle and estrogen levels, which is crucial to women's health. Oviductus Ranae is a natural product for both medicine and food, which has “estrogenic effect”. However, few studies have systematically elaborated its mechanism of action.

pmc-12750904.title: The effect of spraying tryptophan on the physiological characteristics of the periwinkle plant (Catharanthus roseus L.) under drought stress
pmc-12750904.creator: Farshid Yousefi, Alireza Abdali Mashhadi, Amin Lotfi Jalal Abadi, Alireza Shafeinia, Saied Jalily, Narges Soltani
pmc-12750904.description: BackgroundPeriwinkle (Catharanthus roseus L.) is a significant source of two valuable anticancer alkaloids, vincristine and vinblastine. Amino acids serve as precursors for alkaloid biosynthesis, and environmental stresses are known to induce an increase in the ratio of secondary metabolites in plants.

pmc-13225582.title: Co-sleeping as a contributor to early childhood caries: Behavioral pathways and clinical outcomes
pmc-13225582.creator: Gloria Bayón-Hernández, Patricia Solano-Mendoza, Beatriz Solano-Mendoza, Juan Gómez-Salgado, Javier Fagundo-Rivera, Luis El Khoury-Moreno, David Ribas-Pérez
pmc-13225582.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Early childhood caries (ECC) is a multifactorial chronic disease strongly influenced by feeding behaviors and oral hygiene practices. Co-sleeping is a common caregiving practice that may increase ECC risk by facilitating nocturnal feeding and limiting adequate nighttime oral care. This study aimed to evaluate the association between co-sleeping, related behavioral factors, and the presence and severity of ECC in children aged 1 to 6 years. A retrospective observational study was conducted using clinical and radiographic records from a pediatric dentistry clinic.

pmc-13591180.title: An Exploratory Assessment of Service Dog Training for the Treatment of Military Members with Posttraumatic Stress: A Pre-post Interventional Trial
pmc-13591180.creator: Kalyn C Jannace, Michelle Nordstrom, Shannon Fichter, Daniel B Cooper, Rebecca N Schulz, Drake R Ryff, Tiffany Riggleman, David Carlisle, Paul F Pasquina
pmc-13591180.description: ObjectiveTo assess the impact of a Service Dog Training Program (SDTP) on PTSD, anxiety, and depression symptoms among military beneficiaries experiencing PTSD.DesignNonrandomized, nonblinded, pre-post interventional clinical trial conducted between 2019 and 2022; analysis complete 2023.SettingRecruitment, screening, consent, and enrollment were conducted between March 2019 and August 2022.

pmc-13668732.title: Schizophrenia-associated glycoprotein Adamtsl3 regulates perineuronal net formation, maintenance, and adult cortical plasticity
pmc-13668732.creator: Teresa M L Cramer, Saad B Hannan, Lucie Petre, Mark F Bear, Takao K Hensch, Shiva K Tyagarajan
pmc-13668732.description: Perineuronal nets (PNNs) regulate the maturation of parvalbumin-positive (PV+) interneurons during postnatal critical periods and continue to support their function thereafter. Their disruption is implicated in neuropsychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia, yet key endogenous PNN regulators remain unknown. Here, we identify the schizophrenia-associated glycoprotein Adamtsl3 as a PV+ cell-autonomous regulator of PNN integrity.
